name: Makai Beach
description: A new, much-loved beach bar on Arina beach at Kokkini Hani with comfy, affordable sunbeds, good food and coffee, clear water and sunsets. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: The Twins beach bar cafe
description: A beach bar-café on Arina beach with cushioned sunbeds, cocktails, big portions and sunset views. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Nirou Terra
description: A laid-back terraced beach club next to the Minoan villa of Nirou, with ethno music, rag rugs on the sand and an all-day kitchen – sunset with your feet in the sea. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: NAMI Seaside - Bar | Restaurant
description: A beach bar-restaurant on the shallow sandy beach at Gournes, ideal for families and for dinner at dusk as the sun sets over the water. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Coco Bay
description: A simple, budget-friendly beach bar in a small wave-free cove at Gournes with shallow, calm water – perfect for kids. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Noi Noi Cafè & Bar
description: A locals' favourite right by the waves on the Kato Gouves seafront, with good coffee, pizza and friendly service. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: μπαράκι Μαρίας στις Γούβες (mparaki Marias stis Gouves)
description: An alternative, off-the-beaten-track little bar by the sea in Kato Gouves with international music and great cocktails (try the 'Daskalitsa'). Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Yacht Food Lounge Cafè
description: A family restaurant-café on the Kato Gouves shoreline with very good food, sea views and sunsets; open all year.

name: Areya Beach Bar Restaurant
description: An all-day beach bar-restaurant in Analipsi serving sushi and signature cocktails, with a DJ in the evening. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Salty Bar Restaurant
description: A new beach bar-restaurant with earthy Mediterranean flavours in the pretty rocky cove of Sarantari, with crystal-clear water. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: The Ha Beach
description: A small beach bar on a little rocky beach in a quiet spot between Anissaras and Hersonissos, away from the bustle. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Naya seaside experience
description: A new all-day spot on the western Hersonissos beach promenade: breakfast from 8am, sunbeds in the afternoon and dinner at sunset. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Kahlua Beach Bar & Party Restaurant
description: A premium beach bar on Hersonissos' main beach with cabanas, live music and parties, serving food from breakfast to dinner. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Mare Mio - Italian Resto & Beach Bar
description: An Italian restaurant and beach bar on Hersonissos' main beach with fresh pasta, oven-baked pizza and cocktails by the waves. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: King Scorpio Beach Club Restaurant
description: A large beach club across two sandy coves framed by rocks in central Hersonissos, with a pool, nomad-style lounge and restaurant. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Meltemi - Beach Bar Restaurant
description: A beach bar-restaurant on shallow sand at Plaka, east Hersonissos, with a big pool – a good option when the meltemi wind blows (sunbeds charged). Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: NEMO Beach Bar
description: A relaxed beach bar right on the waves in Stalida with excellent cocktails, food and free mini golf – often called the best in Stalida. Seasonal (roughly May–October).
address: Stalis Beach road, Ag. Ioannou 128, Stalis - Heraklion 700 07, Greece

name: Babel Beach Bar
description: A family-run beach bar in central Stalida (Thanis and Maria) with free sunbeds when you order, breakfast, and calm clear water. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Windmill Beach Bar
description: A beach bar with a pool and breakfast on fine sand at west Malia, with cheap umbrellas and free parking. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Nisos Beach Bar Restaurant
description: A tropical boho beach bar on Malia's main beach with beds, palm trees and sushi, looking out to the islet chapel of Agios Pnevmatos. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Dolphin Beach Bar
description: A traditional family beach bar in the best spot on Malia's main beach, serving homestyle Cretan food by shallow water – say hi to Kostas the parrot. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Potamos Beach Restaurant
description: A restaurant serving Potamos beach near Malia, with seafood spaghetti and prawns by shallow blue water, quieter than Malia. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Macao
description: An all-day bar right on the long beach at Kokkinos Pyrgos with cheap sunbeds, good coffee, pancakes and crêpes, and sunsets over the Messara Gulf. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: SEVEN CAFE
description: A bistro-café-wine bar facing the beach at Kokkinos Pyrgos, with free sunbeds when you order; open all year.
address: Παραλιακή, Λεωφ. Κόκκινου Πύργου, Kokkinos Pirgos 702 00, Greece

name: Notia ammos Cafe Snack Bar
description: Often called the best in Kalamaki: coffee and a hearty breakfast through to cocktails, with kids playing in the sand and sunsets over the sea. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Bunga Bunga
description: A legendary, authentic beach bar-taverna on wild Komos beach serving grilled small fish, calamari and dakos; the beach is a protected loggerhead turtle nesting site. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Boho Beach Bar
description: A relaxed all-day beach bar at the end of Matala beach with pancakes, sweets and cocktails, looking at the famous caves. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Music Cafe Bar Matala
description: A bar carved into the rock at the end of Matala beach, with good music, cinnamon lemonade and views of the bay and caves; open in winter with a limited menu.

name: Kahlúa Bar
description: A small, cosy cocktail bar in the lanes by Matala beach, run by welcoming owners Maria and Kostas – perfect for an evening drink. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Blue Cafe Lentas
description: A café in Lentas with nautical décor and aquariums, tasty waffles and coffee, overlooking the bay. Mainly open in season.

name: Tiger Lily Seaview Cafe Bar
description: A café-bar with arguably the prettiest balcony in Lentas, hanging over the sea with panoramic views, and good cocktails. Mainly open in season.

name: Venetia Cafe
description: A family café-snack bar on Tsoutsouros' little harbour with a calm atmosphere, coffee, drinks and snacks. Mainly open in season.

name: ALOS - By The Sea
description: A family café on the shoreline at Kastri (Keratokampos) with homemade sweets, pancakes and waffles by a quiet beach with crystal-clear water. Mainly open in season.

name: EAT Spitikon
description: A raised restaurant-bar overlooking the harbour of Arvi with home-cooked food, breakfast and coffee – the best choice in the village (not a classic beach bar). Mainly open in season.

name: Paraiso Beach Hall
description: A boho beach bar-restaurant on the remote organised beach of Psari Forada, one of the prettiest in southern Crete. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Heraklion Archaeological Museum
description: The world's finest collection of Minoan art: frescoes, the Phaistos Disc and the snake goddesses. Ideally visited after Knossos; free entry on the 1st and 3rd Sunday from November to March.

name: Historical Museum of Crete
description: Crete's story from Byzantine times to today, home to the only El Greco paintings on the island and Kazantzakis' study; the café has a terrace over the sea. Closed Sundays in winter.

name: Natural History Museum of Crete
description: The largest natural history museum in the Mediterranean, on the seafront, with an earthquake simulator and live exhibits – great for families.
address: Κόλπος Δερματά, Leof. Sofokli Venizelou, Iraklio 712 02, Greece

name: Venetian Fortress of Koules
description: The 16th-century Venetian Rocca a Mare fortress guarding the old harbour, with exhibits inside its vaults and a rooftop with panoramic views over the city, port and Aegean. Closed Tuesdays.

name: Nikos Kazantzakis' Grave
description: Nikos Kazantzakis' simple grave on the Martinengo Bastion, inscribed 'I hope for nothing, I fear nothing, I am free', with views over the city and Mt Giouchtas – lovely at sunset; free entry.

name: Morosini Fountain (Liontaria)
description: The Venetian fountain of 1628 with its four lions, the heart of Heraklion – grab a bougatsa or coffee on the square like the locals.

name: Saint Minas Holy Cathedral
description: The imposing cathedral of Heraklion's patron saint, Agios Minas, one of the largest churches in Greece; on 11 November the city celebrates with a grand procession.

name: Museum of Ancient Greek Technology by Kotsanas
description: Working replicas of ancient Greek inventions, from automata to the Antikythera mechanism – ideal for kids and rainy days.

name: Knossos Palace
description: The largest Minoan palace, at the heart of the myth of the Minotaur and the Labyrinth. Arrive at opening time to beat the tour groups.

name: Archaeological Museum
description: A small museum in the heart of Archanes displaying finds from Fourni and Anemospilia – combine it with a stroll through the restored village.

name: Master Christ Church
description: The chapel of Afentis Christos on the summit of Mt Giouchtas, beside a Minoan peak sanctuary, with one of the best views in the prefecture – magical at sunset. Reach it by dirt road or on foot from Archanes.

name: Nikos Kazantzakis Museum
description: The museum dedicated to the life and work of Nikos Kazantzakis, in his ancestral village of Myrtia surrounded by vineyards. Closed Saturdays in winter.

name: Agarathos Monastery
description: One of Crete's oldest monasteries, with an impressive church and small ecclesiastical museum in green countryside; modest dress required.
address: Epar.Od. Karteros - Moni Agkarathou, Moni Agkarathou 700 08, Greece

name: Monastery of Saint George Epanosifis
description: Heraklion's largest monastery, rich in relics and a lively pilgrimage site with views over the hills; closed at midday (around 12:30–17:30), modest dress required.

name: Vrontisi Monastery
description: A 14th-century monastery on the slopes of Mt Psiloritis with frescoes and a famous Venetian marble fountain of Adam and Eve, overlooking the Messara – combine with Lake Votomos and trout in Zaros.

name: CRETAquarium Thalassokosmos
description: A large aquarium of Mediterranean marine life at the former US base in Gournes – a great family outing, best on a weekday morning or a rainy or very hot day.

name: Minoan Palace of Malia
description: The third-largest Minoan palace, set beside the sea with mountain views, home to the famous kernos stone. Closed Tuesdays.

name: Lychnostatis Open Air Museum
description: An open-air folklore museum recreating a traditional Cretan village by the sea, with herbs, looms and workshops; usually open mornings (about 09:00–14:00) – ask about raki and bread workshops.

name: Panagia Kera Kardiotissa Monastery
description: The monastery of Panagia Kera Kardiotissa with its miraculous icon and Byzantine frescoes – a good stop on the mountain road up to the Lasithi Plateau; modest dress required.

name: Minoan Palace of Phaistos
description: The second most important Minoan palace, where the Phaistos Disc was found, with superb views over the Messara plain and Mt Psiloritis; combine with nearby Agia Triada (3 km).

name: Gortyna Archaeological Site
description: The Roman capital of Crete, with the Gortyn Law Code, the odeon and the Basilica of Agios Titos among ancient olive groves; much of the ancient city across the road is free to explore.

name: Caves Matala
description: Rock-cut Roman tombs in the cliffs above Matala bay, the legendary 1960s hippie hideaway, with magical sunsets; small entry fee, usually open until late afternoon.

name: Monastery Panagia Kaliviani
description: A large convent near Moires with beautiful gardens and peacocks, charitable work and a 14th-century church; open most of the day, with a shop selling the nuns' products.
address: Epar.Od. Miron - Pompias, Moni kalivianis 704 00, Greece

name: Odigìtria Monastery
description: A fortified monastery with the Xopateras tower near Agiofarango Gorge, with panoramic views over the Asterousia mountains and Libyan Sea – combine with the gorge hike or a swim at Kali Limenes.

name: Virgin Monastery Koudouma
description: A remote monastery right on the Libyan Sea at the mouth of Katarraktis Gorge, backed by steep mountains; reached by a long, demanding dirt road (about 25 km) – take water and fuel.

name: Swing Thing
description: Crete's top cocktail bar (No. 23 on World's 100 Best Cocktail Bars 2026), with seasonal menus, house infusions and jazz and blues. Few tables, so book ahead; closed Sundays.

name: The Bitters Bar
description: A Prohibition-inspired speakeasy in an arcade behind the Lions fountain, mixing classic cocktails with house-made bitters to a jazz soundtrack; closed Sundays.

name: Xalavro Open Bar
description: An open-air bar in the riad-like courtyard of a ruined 1900s house, with award-winning bartenders, creative cocktails and fusion food.

name: Stone Project
description: An industrial-style cocktail bar on Korai Street serving Mastiha Sours and raki cocktails, with funk, soul and disco DJ sets until late; closed Mondays.

name: Bartenders Club
description: A hidden speakeasy with premium spirits and signature cocktails, one of the city's most serious bars; open only Wednesday–Saturday, so check their social media.

name: Hūmāna
description: The locals' new hot spot on a tree-lined pedestrian street near Agia Aikaterini: spritz, cocktails and pizza, with DJs at weekends.

name: Toucan Skybar
description: A tropical rooftop bar on the 5th floor of a historic building on Eleftherias Square, for sunset cocktails with sweeping views over the square and harbour.

name: 5th CAFE \ BAR
description: A hotel roof bar with signature cocktails and a 180° view over the Aegean, the Venetian harbour and Koules fortress – arguably the best view in the city (a bit pricey).

name: Guernica
description: A classic 35-year-old bar in an old mansion with a lovely garden, good music and occasional live and Cretan music nights.

name: HIGH HOPeS TAPROOM
description: A craft beer taproom with 10 taps and a knowledgeable bartender, a few steps from the seafront – the only one of its kind in the city; no food, closed Sundays.

name: Strafilo Wine & Listening Bar
description: A wine and listening bar south of the centre, pouring natural and Greek wines with quality small plates and curated vinyl; no reservations, closed Sundays.

name: Kelari by Peskesi
description: Peskesi's candlelit stone cellar, with around 130 Cretan wine labels (including rare grape varieties) and Cretan dishes – very romantic.

name: Bofor Music Stage
description: The city's best-known music venue for live Greek and laiko bands, Friday and Saturday until dawn; mainly in the winter season (October–May), booking or minimum spend required.

name: The Dodo Cocktail Bar
description: A relaxed cocktail bar on the seafront with budget-friendly cocktails (try the Mojito Pirata), classic rock and sunset sea views.

name: Ontas Tavern
description: A hidden meze and raki tavern that feels like another era, in a courtyard on an old lane, with traditional meze and frequent live music; opens 20:30, closed Sundays.

name: Palaiino
description: A venue with live Cretan music (lyra and laouto) and food – the best place for a proper Cretan glendi; mainly winter weekends, booking needed, minimum spend around €20 per person.

name: Senses Club
description: A cocktail bar and dance club in Ammoudara with very friendly service, open until 6am. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Pop In Bar - Ammoudara
description: An authentic locals' rock bar in Ammoudara run by Nikos, open in winter too with a fireplace.

name: Theros Beyond the Vine
description: A wine bar in Agia Pelagia with a curated list of local and international wines, chef-made tapas and a captivating view over the bay. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: The Whisky Bar
description: A charming whisky pub by the sea in Kokkini Hani with a huge whisky collection, welcoming owners and sunset views.
address: Beach Road, Kokkini Hani 71500, Heraklion, Crete 151 24, Greece

name: KonDimAr Cocktail Bar
description: A cocktail bar since 1999 in Kato Gouves with premium spirits and fresh herbs from its own garden. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Onar lounge cafe
description: A lounge bar on Kato Gouves' main road since 2000, with live events, dancers and DJs at weekends all year; opens 20:00.

name: Noema Wine Bar
description: A family-run wine bar in a pretty garden in the lanes of Hersonissos, pouring only Greek wines with charcuterie and cold plates. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Pablo Premium Bar
description: A premium cocktail bar with DJs in Hersonissos, ideal for a first drink or an after-party until 5am – a quality alternative to the strip. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: One Way Cocktail Bar
description: A cocktail bar in Koutouloufari with a sunset roof terrace and creative signatures like Alma de Chile and Nut Me. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Dionysos
description: A cosy village bar in Koutouloufari with Cretan hospitality and good cocktails at good prices. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: antidote piskopiano
description: A bar and grill in Piskopiano with top Greek IPAs on tap, cocktails and very good food. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: The Village Inn - Old Hersonissos
description: A small traditional bar on the picturesque square of Old Hersonissos for cocktails, where everyone becomes friends. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: kafenedaki
description: A favourite cocktail bar in Anissaras with a lovely atmosphere, snacks and welcoming owners Maya and Grigoris. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Cosmopolitan Lounge & Bar
description: One of the best bars in Stalida, on the seafront road: a lounge with excellent cocktails and a welcoming host. Seasonal (roughly May–October).
address: Agiou Ioanni 195, Stalida 700 07 Nikos Kazantzakis 2, Agiou Ioanni 195, Stalida 700 07, Greece

name: Whisper Music Cocktail Bar
description: A family-run music cocktail bar in Stalida with great music and fair prices, open until 4am. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Doma bar old town malia
description: A romantic cocktail bar since the late '80s in one of the oldest stone houses in Malia's old village, serving premium cocktails. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Rukuni Garden Cocktail Bar
description: A garden cocktail bar in Malia with sofas among the greenery, chill music and carefully crafted signature cocktails. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Islander cocktail bar
description: A friendly cocktail bar in Malia with '60s–'80s music, mountain views and better, cheaper drinks than the strip. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Hippies Cave Bar&Food
description: A hippie bar-restaurant inside a cave right on the waves in Matala, with chilled music, cocktails and sunset views of the famous caves. Seasonal (roughly May–October).

name: Zelita Winebar
description: A serene café-wine bar on a picturesque lane by the square in Archanes, for wines from local wineries after dinner.

name: Douloufakis Winery
description: Third-generation family winery in Dafnes focused on Vidiano and Liatiko; cellar tour + 6-wine tasting or a vineyard tasting under a pergola with Cretan cheeses.

name: DAF Wines by Douloufaki Fereniki
description: Boutique family winery in the hills of Dafnes; warm hosted tastings (from €18) and vineyard walks, with toys for kids.

name: Amargiotakis Winery
description: Small family winery in Dafnes village; friendly owners host tastings of local Thrapsathiri and Liatiko.

name: Louloudis Winery
description: Century-old family winery (since 1920) in Dafnes; small-scale, best visited by arrangement.

name: Vergitsis winery
description: Authentic small family winery in Dafnes with hospitable hosts.

name: Vorizanakis Winery
description: Family winery founded in 1986 on the Dafnes–Venerato road; known for Muscat of Spina, Liatiko and a celebrated retsina.
address: Επαρχιακή Οδός Δαφνών-Βενεράτου, Provincial Road, Dafnes 700 11, Greece

name: Silva Daskalaki Winery "Biodynamic Farming"
description: Organic & biodynamic family estate in Siva; five different tours, incl. tasting with Cretan cheeses and rusks.

name: IDAIA WINERY
description: Boutique winery of two oenologists (since 2000) championing Vidiano, Vilana, Liatiko & Kotsifali; 4- or 8-wine tastings in the garden.

name: Efrosini Winery
description: Family winery in Kerasia amid vines and olives, partly organic; award-winning wines and very friendly owners.

name: Metaxaris Winery
description: Small multi-generation family winery in Avgeniki with very good prices.

name: Heraklion Winery
description: The historic Heraklion cooperative winery (1927) at Paliani; guided tour of the production area plus tasting programmes from €12.

name: Diamantakis Winery
description: Modern family winery at 450 m at the foot of Psiloritis; award-winning Vidiano & Assyrtiko, excellent guided tastings.

name: PARASKEVAS WINERY
description: Small family winery in Sarchos (Wines of Crete member); neat space and passionate people.

name: Winery Menexes
description: Boutique family winery near Malades, 20 min from the city; hand-made wines and genuine hospitality.

name: Thalassinos Microwinery
description: Family boutique winery on the edge of Heraklion making natural, biodynamic wines in small batches; bookable wine-lover tours.

name: Alexakis S.A. - Alexakis Winery
description: Largest privately owned winery in Crete (1970s), on the city outskirts near Knossos; tasting room in an industrial area.
address: 104-106 Irinis & Filias, Peridi Metohi Heraklion Crete 715 00, Greece

name: Moinoterra Winery
description: Stylish young winery in Archanes reviving old local vineyards; polished guided tastings of native varieties with snacks.

name: Garakis Winery
description: Organic family winery & distillery between Kounavi and Archanes; vineyard tour plus 4–6 wines and raki with local snacks.

name: WINERY STILIANOU
description: Four-generation organic family winery in Kounavi; tastings from €10 with olive oil and local bites, overlooking the vines.

name: Titakis Wines - Fabrika Wine Experience
description: Third-generation winery in the heart of the Peza PDO zone; detailed tour by an oenologist and tasting ("Fabrika Wine Experience").

name: Scalarea Estate
description: The former Boutari Fantaxometocho estate outside Skalani, 8 km from Heraklion; guided tours, 4- or 6-wine tastings, shop and café in a beautiful setting.

name: Mesarmi tasting Crete
description: Tasting room in Houdetsi offering guided tastings of Cretan wines, olive oil and cheese from several producers.
address: Eparchiaki Odos Knossou - Charaka 358, Choudetsi 701 00, Choudetsi 701 00, Greece

name: Digenakis Winery
description: Modern high-tech winery near Kalloni (Peza zone) with an elegant tasting room; also hosts music and art events.

name: Paterianakis Estate
description: Crete's first organic winery (1997), run by the third generation; tastings and a 5-wine food pairing with dishes from the estate garden.

name: Lyrarakis Winery & Tasting Room
description: The flagship Cretan winery that revived Dafni, Plyto and Melissaki; vineyard, cellar & vine-museum tour, tastings with food pairing or vineyard picnic.
address: Alagni, Arkalochori, 70300, Alagni, Heraklion, Crete 703 00, Greece

name: Karapidakis Winery
description: Small family winery in Alagni (official since 2020) known for heartfelt hospitality; tasting of the Iskios range plus home-distilled raki.

name: FRAGOSPITO WINERY
description: Historic organic family estate (roots 1906) in Vorias, the Gavalas family winery; guided winery & cellar tour with tasting of old vintages.

name: Kainourgiakis Family : Winery
description: Boutique family winery in Pyrgos Monofatsiou run by brothers; relaxed seated tastings of native varieties.

name: Zacharioudakis Winery
description: Architecturally spectacular gravity-flow winery on Orthi Petra hill (500 m) above the Messara plain; tours, tastings with Cretan snacks.

name: Raptakis D. Winery & Raki Distillery
description: Family winery and raki still in Moroni; hosts share bread-baking in a wood oven, garden salads, local meat and distillation.

name: Strataridakis bros Winery
description: "Southernmost winery in Europe", with vineyards from the old Agioi Apostoloi monastery; warm family-hosted tastings.

name: Haralabakis Winery
description: Modern family winery in Avli with an elegant tasting hall overlooking the plain; award-winning blends.

name: Agelakis Winery
description: Family winery in the pottery village of Thrapsano (since 2015), also making amphora wines; personal guided tastings.

name: Winery Fournarakis
description: Small family winery & raki distillery in Episkopi; personal tour with grapes, wine and raki tasting.

name: Ammoudara Beach
description: The city beach of Heraklion: a 5 km strip of fine sand with shallow water, beach bars and windsurfing, 10 minutes from town.

name: Paralia Agia Pelagia
description: Sheltered sandy bay in front of the old fishing village; calm water, diving centre and tavernas on the sand.

name: Lygaria beach
description: Small turquoise cove next to Agia Pelagia with clear, calm water, a few tavernas and a diving base.

name: Paralia Mononaftis
description: Narrow, fjord-like inlet on the Agia Pelagia peninsula with deep crystal water – one of the best snorkelling/diving spots on the north coast.

name: Amnissos beach
description: Long sandy beach east of the city with shallow water and the Minoan Villa of the Lilies above it; planes pass overhead on approach.

name: Arena beach
description: The best sandy stretch of Kokkini Hani: lively beach bars, SUP and water sports, popular with young locals.

name: Sarantari Beach
description: Small sandy cove between rocky headlands west of Hersonissos, with clear water and a Blue Flag 2026.

name: Limanakia Beaches
description: A string of tiny rocky coves just west of Hersonissos port – clear water, good snorkelling and a quieter alternative to the town beach.

name: Paralia Stalidas
description: Golden sandy beach with very shallow, calm water – the family-friendly end of the Malia bay.

name: Potamos Beach
description: Malia's most beautiful beach: fine sand and dunes by a small river mouth, far from the party strip, near the Minoan palace.

name: Kokkinos Pyrgos Beach
description: Laid-back fishing-village beach on the Messara bay with shallow water, cafés and fish tavernas – a local family favourite.

name: Kalamaki Beach
description: Long, uncrowded sandy beach in front of a small village, with tavernas on the promenade and great sunsets.

name: Kommos beach
description: Huge golden beach with dunes and tamarisks; Caretta caretta nesting site, Minoan port ruins and spectacular sunsets. North end is naturist-friendly.

name: Matala beach
description: Iconic bay below the cliff caves made famous by the 1960s hippies; organised, deep clear water, legendary sunsets. Very busy in summer.

name: Red beach
description: Wild red-sand cove reached on foot from Matala, framed by ochre cliffs; quieter and wilder than Matala. Naturist-friendly.

name: Vathi Beach
description: Remote, deep sandy bay below the Asterousia cliffs with emerald water – the wild Odigitria coast at its best.
address: Vathi Beach, near Odigitria Monastery 702 00, Greece

name: Agiofaraggo Beach
description: Arguably the most spectacular beach in Heraklion: a pebble cove at the end of a gorge of hermit caves, with turquoise water and a rock arch.
address: Agiofarango Beach, near Odigitria Monastery, Crete, Greece

name: Paralia Ditikos
description: Long, laid-back bay just west of Lentas with clear water and a free-spirited, naturist-friendly vibe.

name: Trafoulas (Psili Ammos) Beach
description: Secluded cove east of Lentas reached through a short gorge; caves, crystal water and very few people.

name: Trypiti beach
description: Wild beach at the end of the Trypiti gorge in the Asterousia mountains; crystal water and a couple of seasonal tavernas.

name: Agios Ioannis Beach
description: Tiny hamlet beach at the mouth of the Goulas gorge below Mt Kofinas: tamarisks, cold clear water, total peace.

name: Paralia Tris Ekklisies
description: Remote fishing hamlet with a pebble beach, fish tavernas and dramatic Asterousia backdrop.

name: Voidomato Beach
description: Hidden cove east of Treis Ekklisies with incredibly deep-blue water; bring supplies.

name: Paralia Agios Nikitas
description: Remote pebble cove below the Agios Nikitas monastery and a hidden palm grove; turquoise water and eagles overhead.

name: Maridaki beach
description: Small pebble beach with crystal water, reached by a long dirt road – loved by locals, with one simple taverna.

name: Paralia Tsoutsouros
description: Relaxed south-coast village beach with a small harbour, tavernas and calm water.

name: Listis Beach
description: Wild, photogenic beach split by a giant boulder, with shallow turquoise water – one of the most beautiful on the south coast.

name: Skouros Beach
description: Quiet sandy bay just west of Kastri with tamarisk shade and an easy sandy entry.

name: Paralia Keratokampou
description: Long, shallow sandy beach in front of a quiet village – ideal for small children.

name: Paralia Arvis
description: Village beach among banana plantations with the Arvi gorge and monastery nearby; clean and calm.

name: Paralia Sindonia
description: Fine-pebble beach with deep, very clear water near Psari Forada; mostly free with a lightly organised section.

name: Tertsa beach
description: Last village of Heraklion to the south-east: long tamarisk-shaded beach, tavernas and a slow pace.

name: Set Sails Crete
description: Relaxed shared sailboat trips from Heraklion's Venetian port to Dia island, with about 4 hours anchored in its clear bays and lunch and drinks included – the best-value Dia cruise.

name: EOS Yachts
description: Newest luxury catamarans in Heraklion with gourmet all-inclusive menu and cocktails; featured by National Geographic Traveler. Ideal for celebrations.

name: Cyma Sails
description: Largest catamaran in Heraklion (Lagoon 500) with a menu by a Top-50 Greek chef; the sunset Dia cruise is a standout.

name: DanEri Yachts
description: Semi-private catamaran cruise to Dia with water slide, sea scooter, SUP, kids options and a nutritionist-designed lunch; very family-friendly.

name: Sailing Crete
description: Long-running sea-sports company; its private 3-hour skippered motorboat cruise explores the coves of Ligaria and Agia Pelagia with snorkelling and fishing.

name: GoFishing Charters
description: Private sport-fishing charters with skipper Konstantinos on a 22-ft boat; families praise grilling the catch on board.

name: Seahorse Rent a boat
description: Affordable 1.5-hour captained tour from Agia Pelagia beach to the Tripiti sea cave and hidden coves, plus no-licence boat rentals.
address: Κυταίου, Αγ. Πελαγία 715 00, Ag. Pelagia 715 00, Greece

name: Dia Private Boat Tours
description: Small private-boat operator in Gouves, the closest eastern harbour to Dia: tailored 4-hour Dia trips, cove-hopping and fishing.
address: Gouves Marina Port, Kato Gouves 700 14, Greece

name: Sea Crete Luxury Escapes
description: Newer luxury boat company (yachts Evgenia ≤8 and Moonlight ≤19) with hotel transfer; Dia catamaran trips with dinner after sunset swims.

name: Fantasia yachting
description: Running since 2004 in Hersonissos: sailing yacht and catamaran cruises with home-made Cretan food, including sunset cruises in St George bay.

name: Agapi Fishing Trips by Captain Nick
description: Authentic working fishing boat of Captain Nick and son Manos (30 years): lay and haul nets, rod fishing and fish identification at sunset. True "live like a local".

name: Vintage Sailing Crete
description: Intimate family-run motor-sailer (≤10 guests) hosted by Yiannis and Iro, with home-made food, olive oil and raki; relaxed morning and sunset trips.

name: Jet Boat Hersonissos
description: High-speed jet-boat ride with spins and sudden stops along the coast, plus a snorkel stop at St George bay – the adrenaline option.
address: port, Agίas Paraskeiis 129, Limenas Chersonisou 700 14, Greece

name: Malia Yachting
description: Friendly sailing catamaran trips that actually depart from Malia, with music, snacks and wine, plus a much-praised sunset tour.

name: SEATRETA - Discover Crete by Sea
description: Premium private boat tours on the Libyan Sea: Paximadia, Matala caves, Agiofarago and Vathi coves only reachable by sea. Covers the Matala gap (no boat operator in Matala itself).

name: Rodanthi Rent Boat
description: No-licence 30 hp boat rental in Kokkinos Pyrgos with a safety briefing and route planning – the easiest way to reach Matala and Red Beach by sea yourself.

name: Antonios Boat Tours | Kaloi Limenes
description: Small family-run boat on the remote south coast: hidden coves, caves, snorkelling, fishing and a home-cooked meal on board.

name: Salty trips (Private cruises—Boat rental)
description: Speedboat excursions along the wild Asterousia coast: sea cave, deserted turquoise beaches only reachable by boat, with captain Marinos and meze.

name: Safari Club Crete
description: The original Crete Land Rover safari (since 2002): small convoys of Defenders with driver-guides into the Lasithi and Dikti mountains, with a long village-taverna lunch and wine.

name: Safari Experts Crete
description: Huge, consistently 5-star jeep operator from Malia mixing off-road driving with real village life: a shepherd farm with goat milking, a cooking lesson and pottery, and a Cretan lunch with wine.

name: Go Crete Safari
description: One of Crete's biggest safari companies, with a fleet of Land Rover Defenders and professional local drivers: Lasithi and Zeus Cave day tours and a popular sunset safari with dinner in a family taverna.

name: Exploring Club Crete
description: For guests who want to drive themselves: small guided convoys of Suzuki Jimnys up to the Lasithi Plateau and Skotino cave, with a village taverna lunch.

name: The Real Safari Crete
description: Young local team with a dedicated family-friendly Lasithi route and a wild south-coast run to Tripiti beach; great value with tastings and a pottery stop.

name: Wild Crete Safari
description: Guided QUAD/buggy option (type: ATV): small groups through olive groves to Skotino cave and Voritsi village; the sunset tour ending at the beach is a favourite.

name: Crete Jeep Safari Adventures
description: The main jeep-safari operator based in Heraklion city: convoys of open jeeps (drive yourself or ride along) across the mountains to a BBQ lunch and a swim on the south coast.

name: Schorsch Guide Touren "the King of Tours" - Private Jeep Safari Touren Kreta (deutschsprachig)
description: Private, German-speaking jeep tours by local Schorsch from his family farm in Rodia: Nida plateau and Anogia BBQ, Giouchtas and Dafnes wines, or a sunrise over Heraklion bay.

name: ELA Quad Safari Crete
description: Outstanding guided QUAD tour (type: ATV) on the west side of Heraklion: off-road trails above Agia Pelagia, the abandoned village of Achlada and sunset over Fodele bay.
address: Unnamed Road, Mononaftis 715 00, Ag. Pelagia 715 00, Greece

name: South Crete Safari
description: Small family-run jeep safari in the south: the only top operator based in Messara, taking guests from Matala up Psiloritis to Anogia or along the wild Asterousia coast.

name: Stay Wet Diving Center
description: Heraklion’s benchmark dive centre since 1995, a PADI 5-Star resort right on the crystal-clear, sheltered Mononaftis bay with reefs, caves and wrecks a short swim away.

name: Poseidon Diving Club Crete
description: A small SSI/ANDI dive centre on quiet Mades Bay next to Agia Pelagia: relaxed beach-entry try dives and snorkelling, plus a cave and a shipwreck for certified divers.

name: Eurodiving
description: The all-round sea-activities base on Ligaria beach: calm-water SUP and kayak for beginners, windsurf, e-foil and wing-foil sessions, plus beginner scuba and snorkelling.

name: Enjoy-Crete
description: Crete’s leading sea-kayak outfitter runs a guided day paddle from Pantanassa to Agia Pelagia: rock formations, a sea cave, remote coves and snorkel stops. No experience needed (8+).

name: Eco Diving Center
description: SSI 5-Star and Blue Oceans dive centre in Ammoudara, convenient for guests staying in or near Heraklion city. Small groups, beginner try dives and boat dives on the north coast.
address: Leof. Andrea Papandreou 137, Ag. Dimitrios 714 14, Greece

name: iKiTe ~ Iraklio Kite Club
description: Heraklion’s first and only licensed kite station (since 2015), with a dedicated sandy kite beach away from swimmers. IKO-certified lessons, wing foil and windsurf in the summer meltemi.

name: Time2Try - Water Sports
description: Friendly lifeguard-run watersports hut on long sandy Amnissos beach, 10 minutes from Heraklion: jet ski, canoe out to Karteros islet, SUP and inflatables for families.

name: Surf In Crete
description: Award-winning IKO/ASI watersports academy on Arina beach run by ASI world trainer Marios Trigonis: private surf, SUP, kite, wing and windsurf lessons with its own rescue tower.

name: Horizon Diving
description: Perfect-scoring, small-group dive operator that collects guests from hotels from Agia Pelagia to Malia and takes them to Mononaftis or the Byron I wreck off the south coast.

name: Aris Water Sports
description: A leading beach watersports centre on Analipsi beach: parasailing, jet ski, flyboard, wakeboard and family inflatables, with a safety-first crew. Seasonal.

name: CORAL Diving Center Crete
description: Family-run PADI 5-Star centre on the beach at Anissaras with 30+ years of experience and new Scubapro gear; daily boat dives and the best-loved beginner dives on the east coast.
address: In front of the LAGUNA SPA RESORT HOTEL (on the beach, Chersonisos 700 14, Greece

name: Duos Water Sports
description: A beach station on the sheltered Creta Maris bay in Hersonissos: walk off your sunbed for jet ski, flyboard, wakeboard or a paddle, always with a rescue jet ski on the water. Seasonal.

name: Heraklion Diving Center - Hersonissos Crete
description: An SSI dive school in Hersonissos with daily small-group boat dives to local sites and very gentle first-time try dives from the beach.

name: Skyride Watersports
description: Family-run beach station on Stalis beach best known for its smooth parasailing flights over Malia bay, plus jet skis and banana/sofa rides for groups.

name: Dolphin Water Sports Malia
description: Malia’s original watersports centre (since 1980) on the main beach, with the widest menu on the coast, from parasailing and flyboard to jetpack and wakeboard.
address: Main beach of Malia, Armirolakou street, Malia 700 07, Greece

name: Diving center The sea lovers
description: A standout dive centre on the south coast: scuba and freediving in the clear Libyan Sea near Kaloi Limenes, including the Byron I shipwreck tour.

name: MARE SUD Diving Center & Boat Rental
description: Long-running (1992) dive centre in Kokkinos Pyrgos: dives at 14 Messara sites and a much-loved day trip to the uninhabited Paximadia islands with snorkelling and a beach BBQ.

name: Finikia Horseriding
description: A family-run riding farm in the hills just outside Heraklion with calm, well-cared-for horses matched to your level: mountain rides with city-and-sea views and sunrise canters on Ammoudara beach, followed by a home-cooked Cretan meal.
address: Κεντρο Ιππασιας Φοινικια Μικρας Ασιας, ταχυδρομικη, θυριδα 613, Finikia 715 00, Greece

name: Riding Academy Crete
description: Heraklion's historic riding centre (since 1979) inside the green Amnisiades Park estate near the airport: small-group beach rides into the waves at Amnisos, gorge trails, pony rides and lessons, plus a café and petting farm that make it an easy family outing.

name: Arion Stables & Apartments Hersonissos
description: A family-run stable (George & Zara) in the hills of Ano Hersonissos, known for impeccably kept horses: quiet rides through vineyards and olive groves with sea views, sunrise beach rides, romantic horse-carriage trips to Analipsi at sunset, and a wood-oven taverna on site.

name: Thalori Horseriding Crete
description: Authentic horse trekking from the Thalori eco-village in the wild Asterousia mountains (UNESCO biosphere reserve): guide Lea leads small groups to the Kofinas summit, down Tripiti Gorge to the Libyan Sea, or on a 2-hour sunrise ride with sweeping south-coast views.

name: Barbarigos Pâtisserie & Café
description: Heraklion's oldest patisserie (family business since the 1930s, under this name since 1964), famous across Crete for its secret-recipe chocolate 'truffles' – soft chocolate-glazed cream bites in dozens of flavours.

name: Aretousa Cretan Handmade Delicacies
description: A small shop of handmade Sitia-style Cretan sweets steps from the 1866 market: kalitsounia, honey-drenched xerotigana and festive cookies, praised for genuine homemade flavour – the place to taste (and take home) traditional Cretan sweets.

name: Solo Gelato
description: Widely called the best gelato in Heraklion: natural, Italian-style gelato with Cretan twists (honey & soft cheese, feta, mascarpone-fig), on a quiet street just off the main pedestrian drag.

name: Gloria Patisserie
description: A Heraklion favourite since 1965 with 150+ traditional and modern sweets; its award-winning galaktoboureko is often called the best in Crete.

name: Emmanouil Patisserie
description: A minimalist, top-tier modern patisserie that locals compare with the best in Athens and abroad: jewel-like chocolates in daring flavours (whisky & salt, ouzo), caramel choux and refined cakes.

name: Giannarakis Ice cream
description: A Heraklion ice-cream maker that locals swear by: old-school fresh-milk ice cream in 40+ flavours (the pistachio is famous) and handmade kataifi. Seasonal – roughly April to late September.

name: Stella's Ice cream
description: A neighbourhood ice-cream shop making everything from fresh milk (incl. goat's milk) with no cream, powders, stabilisers or ready-made bases – many locals call it the best ice cream in Heraklion.

name: Pulp Gelato
description: A Hersonissos gelateria making gelato daily from pure Greek and Cretan ingredients – try the pistachio, Biscoff or Greek-yogurt flavours; good vegan options too.

name: Koula Cretan Gelato
description: A one-of-a-kind gelateria using Cretan goat's milk: rich, creamy and slightly tangy gelato (tiramisu, salted caramel, pistachio) – free tastings and a hit with visitors who can't take cow's milk.

name: Steam Single Origin Coffees
description: Heraklion's reference single-origin coffee bar: beans roasted in-house, filter and espresso dialled in daily, and bags of whatever origin is pouring that week to take home. Handy stop on the way to/from the airport.

name: Koul Microbakery
description: Tiny micro-bakery and specialty coffee spot in a lane beside the Agios Minas cathedral: espresso, filter and cold brew with fresh pastries, sourdough bakes and deli goods – mostly to go, locals perch on the steps.
address: Gerasimou Pardali, Ag. Mina &, Iraklio 712 01, Greece

name: Speira
description: A bookshop-café with floor-to-ceiling shelves and a quiet upstairs room for reading or laptop work, tables outside looking onto the Agios Minas cathedral; good coffee and homemade cakes (try the carrot cake).

name: Hacienda Experience
description: The original 2013 Hacienda, the café that kick-started Heraklion's specialty-coffee scene: Taf-roasted house blend plus rotating micro-lots, homemade sweets and a big all-day menu in a leafy Mastabas setting.

name: ML Espresso bar
description: Small, much-loved espresso bar under the Megaro Ntore on Eleftherias Square: specialty espresso and flat whites, single-origin Ethiopia, proper Greek coffee and quick fresh snacks. Ideal stop before the Archaeological Museum.
address: Μέγαρο Ντορέ, Plateia Eleftherias 29-31, Iraklio 712 02, Greece

name: Cafe BITE
description: Friendly corner café above the old Venetian harbour with a direct view of the Koules fortress and the marina – homemade cakes, pies and fresh juices with your freddo; the nicest harbour-view coffee in town.

name: Coco Blanc Coffee & Decor
description: Owner-run specialty café inside a pretty home-decor and plant boutique on pedestrian Chandakos Street: good coffee, a light healthy brunch and a calm, beautifully styled space. Closes early evening and on Sundays.

name: Auto Stop Cafe
description: A 36-year-old Ammoudara institution run by the ever-smiling Mario and family: Greek coffee or freddo always arrives with a slice of homemade cake, plus great pistachio ice cream, pool table and football on screen.
address: Leof. Andrea Papandreou 161, Ag. Dimitrios 714 14, Greece

name: Cherry Beans - Speciality Coffee
description: Small specialty-coffee bar on the main road opposite Eri beach – the one place in Hersonissos for a properly made espresso, cappuccino or decaf (try their "Explorer" beans) and creative cold drinks.
address: Main road, in front of eri beach, Limenas Chersonisou 700 14, Greece

name: Two Waves
description: Bright sea-view café on Stalida's beach road: good coffee, sandwiches, homemade ice cream and frozen yogurt by day, cocktails in the evening – all looking out over the bay.

name: Smile Cafe
description: Beachfront terrace café over Matala bay, looking across to the famous caves: breakfast and coffee in the morning, smoothies by day and one of the best sunset seats in Matala.

name: KOULE CAFE BAR RESTAURANT
description: A green oasis in Messara: café-restaurant inside the shady pine grove of Koule hill in Moires, with a playground for kids – good coffee and meals in the trees, a welcome break on the way to Phaistos or Matala.
